items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Didn't they have any good clarinet players around New York, Michael?

ctx.x: And all the fans, of course, know why they couldn't play him. So, and the rest would say, oh, come on, man, stop all this. And I said, okay. And I came back in the band, stayed in 1940. Yeah.
Didn't they have any good clarinet players around New York, Michael?

They were, they were, they were play parts. They were pretty sad, but you had no one, no soul. You know, Barnaby Gardner and I, I think the two, two best ones around New York at the time. Yeah, I don't tell you.
